result.summary: Adds support for "never" as a valid value for the `timestamp` parameter in the `importdescriptors` RPC. Descriptors imported with `timestamp: "never"` do not trigger a blockchain rescan, allowing wallets to bypass scanning entirely if no other descriptors require it. The change also adds explicit validation rejecting negative numeric timestamps.
result.problem: Previously, `importdescriptors` required an integer timestamp or "now". Specifying "now" still initiated a rescan over the timestamp window (the last two hours and the mempool), imposing unnecessary scanning latency when importing descriptors known to be new or when users intend to defer rescanning.
evidence: The PR author cites issue #31263 in the description: 'Fix related to issue: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/31263'.
result.card: Adds a "never" option to the timestamp parameter in importdescriptors, enabling users to completely skip the blockchain rescan during descriptor import. Currently, specifying "now" still forces a rescan over the two-hour timestamp window and the mempool, causing unnecessary delay when importing fresh descriptors or when callers prefer to rescan manually later. The PR also explicitly rejects negative timestamps with an RPC error. Motivation is linked to issue #31263.
